meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Rule No. 1: Never lose money. Rule No. 2: Never forget rule No. 1'?
meta.ogDescription: Buffett's idea, but not his sentence. Wikiquote calls the numbered Rule No. 1 wording Disputed; the checkable version appears in Forbes, 23 Sept 2010.

answer.label: Not Buffett’s wording — a polished paraphrase of his rule
answer.authorDates: Born 30 August 1930 · investor and chairman of Berkshire Hathaway
answer.sourceLine: The idea is genuinely Buffett’s, but the tidy numbered sentence is not traceable to anything he is documented as saying or writing. Wikiquote files this exact wording under Disputed and points instead to a checkable version Buffett spoke in Omaha, printed by Forbes on 23 September 2010: “The first rule is don’t lose, and the second rule is never forget the first rule.”

source.excerpt: The first rule is don’t lose, and the second rule is never forget the first rule. It isn’t so much having a lot of brilliant decisions, it’s just not having some terrible ones.
trail: Searched Quote Investigator’s Warren Buffett investigations ↗ and its site search: no article on this line exists, so there is no QI ruling to adopt or contradict.

Read the wikitext of Wikiquote’s Warren Buffett page ↗ directly. The numbered wording sits in the Disputed section, described as “widely attributed” and “perhaps of gambling or horse racing origin,” with the Forbes variant named as the version with greater checkability.
Fetched the Forbes article of 23 September 2010 ↗ and confirmed it carries Buffett’s unnumbered wording of the rule, in his own voice.

Checked the catalogue record for Mary Buffett and David Clark’s The Tao of Warren Buffett ↗, confirming Scribner, 2006 — the collection Wikiquote names. No searchable full text is available through that record, so no page citation is claimed here.
source.excerptNote: This is Buffett’s own wording as Forbes printed it, from a conversation recorded at his office in Omaha. Note what it does not contain: no numbering, and not the phrase “never lose money.”

author.name: Warren Buffett
author.heading: Who Warren Buffett is
author.metaLine: Born 30 August 1930 · American investor · chairman of Berkshire Hathaway since 1970
author.bio: Warren Buffett was born in Omaha on 30 August 1930 and went to Columbia specifically to study under Benjamin Graham, the father of value investing, later working at Graham’s partnership from 1954 to 1956. He has been chairman of Berkshire Hathaway since 1970, and his annual letters to shareholders — published openly since 1977 — are the largest body of writing he has actually signed his name to. Buffett is a genuinely quotable speaker, which is precisely why so many improved versions of his lines circulate under his name.

cite.sourceCitation: Warren Buffett, quoted in “Jay-Z, Buffett and Forbes on Success and Giving Back,” Forbes, 23 September 2010: “The first rule is don’t lose, and the second rule is never forget the first rule.” The numbered “Rule No. 1 / Rule No. 2” wording is listed under “Disputed” at Wikiquote, s.v. “Warren Buffett,” which notes it was attributed to him by Mary Buffett and David Clark in The Tao of Warren Buffett (Scribner, 2006).

misattribution.heading: What’s actually wrong here
misattribution.intro: This is not a fabrication pinned on a stranger. The rule really is Buffett’s — the famous numbered sentence is a tidier restatement that nobody has traced back to him.

items.why: Wikiquote places “Rule No. 1: Never lose money. Rule No. 2: Never forget rule No. 1.” in its Disputed section ↗, describing it as “widely attributed” to Buffett and “perhaps of gambling or horse racing origin.” No speech, letter, interview or annual report of his has been found containing it.

items.who: Mary Buffett and David Clark, The Tao of Warren Buffett
items.why: Wikiquote notes the maxim was attributed to Buffett — “perhaps facetiously” — by his former daughter-in-law Mary Buffett in this quotation collection, published by Scribner in 2006 ↗. Wikiquote does not claim the book invented the line, only that it is a notable place the attribution appears in print.

Worth knowing before you trust a confident answer elsewhere: QI has traced many Buffett lines, but this rule is not among its investigations ↗. Anyone citing a precise first utterance for it is not citing QI.

misattribution.truthLine: What Buffett is actually documented saying is “The first rule is don’t lose, and the second rule is never forget the first rule” ↗ — the same idea, unnumbered, and without the words “never lose money.”

context.heading: Why the fake version travels further
lead: Buffett actually said the thing — just not this way. In a filmed Omaha conversation printed by Forbes, he put it as “The first rule is don’t lose, and the second rule is never forget the first rule,” and immediately explained what he meant: “It isn’t so much having a lot of brilliant decisions, it’s just not having some terrible ones.” That is a working investor describing loss aversion, not a slogan.

The numbered version is what happens when a good line gets edited for the poster. Adding “Rule No. 1” and “Rule No. 2” turns a remark into a commandment, and swapping “don’t lose” for “never lose money” makes it sound absolute — which is the one thing Buffett, who has written candidly about his own losses, has never claimed.
context.detailsSummary: Where to look for what Buffett really wrote
detailsBody: Buffett’s annual letters to Berkshire Hathaway shareholders ↗ are posted free by the company and cover 1977 through 2024. They are the single largest body of prose Buffett has signed, and the obvious first stop for anyone trying to source a line credited to him.
Wikiquote’s note that the maxim may be “of gambling or horse racing origin” is a suggestion, not a documented finding — no earlier claimant has been established, and quotle.info does not assert one.
context.pull: Buffett’s point survives the rewrite. His phrasing didn’t.
